**Stretched 4:3, dual-mode monitors and up to 480 fps.**

**Download:** `ClipRing-v0.1.1-win-x64.zip` below, unzip, start `ClipRing.exe`. No installation; .NET and FFmpeg are included. Your settings from 0.1.0 are kept.

### New
- **4:3 stretched:** if you play stretched (e.g. 1280 × 960 or 1440 × 1080 in CS2), clips are stretched to your screen's format, the way they looked on your monitor. On by default (**Video → Stretch 4:3 and other formats to the screen format**).
- **Dual-mode monitors:** ClipRing notices when your monitor switches modes (e.g. 4K 240 Hz ↔ 1080p 480 Hz) and remembers frame rate and resolution for each mode.
- **Up to 480 fps** (was 240).

### Fixed
- When the monitor resolution went back up (e.g. after leaving a game), the recording kept the lower resolution.
- Alt-tabbing out of a game with its own resolution no longer restarts the recording, so the replay buffer is kept.
- Scaled recordings (lower resolution than the monitor) now stay on the graphics card on more systems instead of falling back to the CPU.

The download now also contains `FFMPEG-SOURCE.txt` with the exact sources of the included FFmpeg.

Windows may warn because the program is not signed yet: click **More info → Run anyway**.
